description:
Gap. A long-running tractable-mcp keeps the code it started with, but the package on disk can change under it: `uv tool upgrade tractable`, or a project's `uv run --locked` syncing a new vendored wheel into its venv. Observed 2026-11-13: a BenchBox server started at 08:16 still ran 1.1.0 (and accepted the prefix expect_store "BenchBox-dev/Bench") because the venv moved to 1.1.1 at 08:20. The same happened to the global servers after the 1.1.1 upgrade on 2026-11-12. The todo skill 4.1.0+ now tells agents to compare tractable_batch.tool_version with the project's pinned runtime, but that is a manual check that needs the agent to know the pin. The server can detect the simplest case itself: its own installed distribution version (importlib.metadata, read fresh) differs from the version it loaded at startup.

Decision gate (implementer proposes, owner confirms before merge): when the versions differ, either (a) get_instructions and every write response carry a warning naming both versions and the restart instruction, or (b) writes are refused with a gate-kind code until restart while reads keep working. Recommendation to weigh: (a) first, because a mixed-version server is not known to corrupt state and (b) can strand a session mid-claim.

Guardrails:
- No state-schema change and no change to claim or publication semantics.
- The check reads only the server's own installed metadata; it never inspects other processes or projects' pins.
- Its cost stays negligible per call (cache the result for a short interval, at most one metadata read per few seconds).
- A missing or unreadable metadata entry yields no warning, never a refusal.
